metaDescription: Six wide corded dethatcher-scarifiers under $500, 15 to 16 inches, with 13 to 15 amp motors, compared on depth range, tines, bags and ownership.
expertTake: The WEN DT1516 is the best overall for its 15-amp motor, 16-inch path and five depth positions. The LawnMaster GVB1316 is the value pick if a 13-amp motor is enough. Anyone whose lawn is over half an acre should skip corded machines and rent a gas power rake.
introParagraphs: Raising the budget cap to $500 does not buy a different kind of machine, because corded electric dethatchers all share the same architecture. What it buys is width, current and finer controls, so this guide concentrates on the upper end of the corded range.

Prices move, and the cap reflects listing prices when this guide was updated. The real question at this level is whether you need a wider head at all, or whether a cheaper narrow machine would finish the same lawn with a little more patience. That honest framing guides the picks below: wider and stronger is not automatically better.

products.name: WEN DT1516 16-Inch 15 Amp Dethatcher Scarifier
products.description:
The WEN DT1516 pairs a 15-amp motor with a 16-inch path, which is the practical ceiling for a corded machine on a 15-amp household circuit. It turns the reel at up to 3,300 RPM and carries a 20-blade scarifying head for the second job. The five depth positions span from a quarter inch above the soil line to half an inch below it, so the range covers light moss combing through to a shallow overseeding cut.

Against the 13-amp LawnMaster at the same 16-inch width, the WEN has two more amps of reserve, which shows when thatch is thick and the reel starts to bog. The trade is the circuit: 15 amps leaves no room to share a breaker with a garage freezer or a second tool, and the cord must be a heavy outdoor gauge.

WEN is known for straightforward parts and manuals, and the machine disassembles with ordinary hand tools. Clear the reel after each session, check the bag zipper, and keep the cord behind you. It is the machine to pick for a half-acre-or-smaller lawn where one machine must do everything.
products.bestFor: Lawns up to about half an acre where thick thatch calls for the most corded power.
pros: 15-amp motor gives the most reserve in the group
Includes both dethatching and 20-blade scarifying heads
Straightforward parts support from a known brand
cons: Uses nearly all of a 15-amp circuit

products.name: LawnMaster GVB1316 16-Inch 13 Amp Dethatcher
products.description:
LawnMaster fits a 16-inch head to a 13-amp motor, which keeps the amperage below the full circuit limit while keeping the path as wide as the WEN. The reel reaches up to 3,700 RPM, the fastest no-load figure here, though the rated amps rather than that speed decide how it behaves under load.

Its 12-gallon bag is close to the 13.2 gallons on the SENIX and larger than the Sun Joe AJ805E bag in this price bracket, so the cleanup rhythm is good. The listing itself notes the motor gives adequate power for some dethatching and scarifying jobs, which is an honest hint: on dense, spongy thatch you will make several shallow passes rather than one deep one.

The typical weaknesses of a budget-brand wide machine apply: confirm that replacement tines are available and that the reel nut stays tight. For a lawn with moderate thatch it is the best use of money in this group.
products.bestFor: Wide-path coverage without paying for the maximum 15-amp motor.
pros: Lower circuit draw than the 15-amp WEN
cons: 13 amps has less reserve in dense thatch
Listing is cautious about heavy-duty work

products.name: DEKOPRO 15-Inch 15 Amp Dethatcher Aerator
products.description:
The DEKOPRO combines a 15-amp copper motor at up to 3,500 RPM with a 15-inch reel and five positions spanning minus 11 millimetres to plus 10 millimetres. That is a precisely stated range, a point in its favor because many listings only say adjustable.

On paper it matches the WEN on current, with an inch less width. The difference is brand maturity: DEKOPRO is a newer name, so parts, manuals and long-term track record are less certain than for WEN or Sun Joe. Treat early ownership as a trial, keep spare hardware, and register the purchase.

It makes sense for buyers who want 15-amp power at a competitive price and are comfortable with a less-established brand. Handle it like any 15-amp machine: heavy cord, no shared circuit, empty the bag often. One practical note on the DEKOPRO: because the listing is newer, read the manual for the warranty terms before you commit, and photograph the reel layout before the first teardown. If the motor or reel develops a problem in the first season, a clear purchase record speeds up any claim. Use a 14 gauge outdoor cord of modest length and store the machine with the bag dry and the tines clear of debris.
products.bestFor: Buyers wanting 15 amps with a clearly stated depth range.
pros: Clearly stated -11 mm to +10 mm range
Five depth positions for fine control
cons: Newer brand with uncertain parts support
Reel is one inch narrower than the WEN

products.name: Sun Joe AJ805E 15-Inch 13 Amp Dethatcher
products.description:
The Sun Joe AJ805E uses a 13-amp motor on a 15-inch reel, with a five-position depth lever and a scarifier blade reel in the box. Sun Joe is one of the longest-established names in budget corded yard tools, and that shows in how easy it is to find manuals, bags and replacement reels.

Compared with the AJ798E in the lower tier, this model gains width and amperage, and it covers roughly twenty percent more ground per pass. Compared with the WEN it gives up two amps and an inch.

Maintenance is routine: clear the reel, inspect the cord and store it dry. If after-sale support matters to you, this is the machine to prefer over a lesser-known import at the same power. At year three, the usual wear items on a Sun Joe are the tines and the bag zipper, both inexpensive and easy to source. A light coat of oil on the reel shaft area and a dry shed keep corrosion away. For a homeowner who dethatches once a year, that low-drama ownership is worth more than a couple of extra amps.
products.bestFor: Owners who value brand support and parts availability.
pros: Established brand with readily available spares
Blade reel included in the box
cons: Bag is smaller than larger-bag rivals

products.name: Westinghouse 16-Inch 15 Amp Dethatcher
products.description:
The Westinghouse 16-inch matches the WEN's 15 amps and 16 inches, with 24 spring tines on the dethatching reel and a 20-blade scarifier. The five depth positions run from -0.5 to +0.25 inch, the same half-inch overall span as the WEN but shifted a little toward cutting.

Its selling point over the WEN is reel layout: more tines means a denser comb, so each pass lifts more fine thatch and leaves a cleaner surface. That also means a bit more drag, so lean on the 15-amp reserve.

Maintenance and cord needs are the same as the WEN. Either is a good buy; choose the Westinghouse for the denser tine count and the WEN for the better-known brand. The heavier tine layout also means the reel bites harder, so mow the grass short and make the first pass at the shallowest setting. Expect to empty the bag more often than on a lighter-combing machine, because it pulls out more fine material per pass.
products.bestFor: Lawns where a clean finish matters more than raw speed.
pros: 24 spring tines lift fine thatch thoroughly
cons: Newer brand than WEN or Sun Joe

products.name: SENIX 15-Inch 13 Amp 2-in-1 Dethatcher
products.description:
The SENIX is the pick for owners who hate emptying the bag, holding 13.2 gallons against 12 on the LawnMaster. Its 24 spring-steel tines at 1.5 mm are a sturdier build than thin-wire reels.

The motor is 13 amps, so it trails the 15-amp group in thick thatch, and the four depth positions are coarser than the five-step levers of the WEN, DEKOPRO and Westinghouse. It is a sensible choice if you work a lawn in long, patient sessions.

Keep tines clean and bags dry. Spare tines are individually replaceable. In year three the likely maintenance items are bag zipper wear and individual tine replacement, both easy jobs. Store it hung on a wall hook with the bag dry, and the 13-amp motor will outlast the tines on a typical suburban lawn.
products.bestFor: Long sessions where fewer bag stops matter more than peak power.
pros: Biggest bag in the group at 13.2 gallons
13-amp motor is easier on the circuit
cons: Less motor reserve than the 15-amp models

buyingCriteria.explanation: A 15-amp motor such as the WEN or DEKOPRO has two amps more reserve than the 13-amp LawnMaster or SENIX. It only matters if thatch is thick, because light thatch does not load the motor. The cost of 15 amps is a circuit with no room for anything else, so use a heavy outdoor cord.

A 16-inch path on the WEN covers about six percent more ground than a 15-inch SENIX, but wider reels fill the bag faster. The SENIX 13.2 gallons against the Sun Joe AJ805E means longer runs between stops. Match the bag to the lawn, not only to the path.

Listings that only say adjustable are a red flag. The DEKOPRO states -11 mm to +10 mm and the WEN states +1/4 to -1/2 inch. A narrow range cannot both rake moss and cut grooves. Always begin at the shallowest setting.
More tines comb finer but drag more. The Westinghouse has 24 spring tines and the SENIX has 24 at 1.5 mm. Fewer, stiffer tines remove coarse thatch faster, while denser reels leave a cleaner finish.

At this level the motors are alike, so parts availability separates the machines. Sun Joe and WEN have deeper supply chains than newer names like DEKOPRO. Check the cost of replacement tines and a bag before buying.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Do you need a wide head?
buyingCriteria.explanation: A 16-inch head only saves time on open turf. On a small or bed-heavy lawn, the narrower reel scalps edges when tilted. If the lawn is under 5,000 square feet, a 13-inch machine from a lower budget tier would likely do the job as well.

specDecoder.meaning: Current draw at full load, a proxy for torque on a corded motor.
specDecoder.watchFor: The WEN and DEKOPRO list 15 amps, the LawnMaster and SENIX 13.

specDecoder.meaning: Reel speed without resistance. Real speed drops with thatch drag.
specDecoder.watchFor: The LawnMaster lists 3700 RPM, but the 15-amp WEN lists 3300 and may cut better.

specDecoder.meaning: The vertical distance the reel can travel above and below the soil line.
specDecoder.watchFor: The WEN spans a quarter inch above to half an inch below ground.

specDecoder.meaning: Number of spring tines on the dethatching reel. More tines comb finer.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Westinghouse and SENIX both list 24 tines.

specDecoder.meaning: Gallons the bag holds before it must be emptied.
specDecoder.watchFor: The SENIX is the biggest at 13.2 gallons.

howWeEvaluated.title: Power versus circuit
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared amps against the 15-amp circuit limit. The WEN and DEKOPRO use nearly all of a circuit, while the LawnMaster, Sun Joe and SENIX sit at 13 amps. We credited reserve but penalized machines that leave no margin.

howWeEvaluated.title: Depth precision
howWeEvaluated.description: We read depth specs for positions and range. The DEKOPRO's -11 mm to +10 mm range was clearer than listings that state nothing.

howWeEvaluated.title: Reel construction
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked tine counts and materials. The SENIX 1.5 mm and Westinghouse 24-tine reels scored well.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cleanup
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared bag volumes and ease of removal.

howWeEvaluated.title: Support
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at brand maturity and spare parts, giving Sun Joe and WEN credit.

cards.label: 13 amp
cards.text: The LawnMaster, Sun Joe AJ805E and SENIX are easier on circuits and sufficient for moderate thatch.

cards.label: 15 amp
cards.text: The WEN, DEKOPRO and Westinghouse have the reserve for dense mats but draw almost a full circuit.

howToChoose.note: Pick 13 amps for a typical lawn, 15 for a neglected one.

rows: Willing to trial a newer brand

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A scarifier reel with a shallow, controllable depth, so the blades open the soil without tearing out crowns.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The DEKOPRO with its stated -11 to +10 mm range and the WEN with its five steps are the best for this.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: The lawn is a quarter acre or more, thatch is thick, and you want the WEN over the SENIX.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Thatch is light and the lawn modest, so the SENIX or LawnMaster will suffice.

maintenance.why: Packed thatch holds moisture and rusts tines.
Bent tines damage turf; replace them individually.
A nicked cord is a shock risk.

faq.q: Is it worth paying more for 15 amps?
faq.a: If thatch is thick, yes, since reserve means one deep pass instead of several. For light thatch the 13-amp machines do the same job.

faq.q: What does a higher cap buy over a cheaper dethatcher?
faq.a: Mostly width and current. Prices move and the cap reflects listing prices when this guide was updated, and the machines are the same type as cheaper ones.

faq.q: Will a 16-inch machine fit a small lawn?
faq.a: It will, but it is awkward around beds and edges. A narrower machine suits a small lawn better.

faq.q: Does a higher RPM dethatch better?
faq.a: No. RPM is no-load speed. Motor amps and tine design decide performance under load.

faq.q: When is the best time to dethatch?
faq.a: When grass is actively growing: early fall for cool-season, late spring for warm-season.

faq.q: How do I avoid scalping the lawn?
faq.a: Mow short first, begin at the shallowest setting, and step down only if thatch remains.
